title: God everywhere; things in God; Parmenides answered
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): our grasp, when rather things stand as in GOD, out from whom, through whom, plus in whom stand as all things in Romans 11:36 plus Acts 17:25, 27-28. But God stands as said unto be everywhere unto ye measure belonging toward Parmenides argues: it stands as in no wise in itself, nor in another. If ye One stands as, we say God stands as in Himself according unto our mode belonging toward understanding, plus we explain it negatively: But that does in no wise strike us, because Himself, that stands as, in no wise in another. God stands as in attributes unto God that He fills heaven plus earth. Yet Jeremiah 23:24 also because each sense stands as true: Scripture teaches both, toward God, this one more fitted unto our intelligence. that one worthier belonging
pass_b_english: But God is said to be everywhere to the measure of our grasp, when rather things are in GOD, from whom, through whom, and in whom are all things in Romans 11:36 and Acts 17:25, 27-28.

Parmenides argues: If the One is, it is not in itself, nor in another. But that does not strike us, because we say God is in Himself according to our mode of understanding, and we explain it negatively: God is in Himself, that is, not in another. Yet Jeremiah 23:24 also attributes to God that He fills heaven and earth. Scripture teaches both, because each sense is true: that one worthier of God, this one more fitted to our intelligence.
source_text: Esse autem ubique dicitur Deus ad modulum captus nostri, cum potius res sint in DEO, ex quo, per quem et in quo omnia, Rom. XI.36. Act. XVII.25,27,28. Parmenides arguit: Si unum est, non est in se, neque in alio. Sed illud nos non ferit, quia Deum dicimus esse in se secundum nostrum intelligendi modum, et exponimus negative, Deum esse in se, id est, non in alio. Jeremias tamen etiam XXIII.24. Deo tribuit, quod caelum ac terram impleat. Utrumque vero Scriptura docet, quia uterque sensus est verus: ille dignior Deo, hic vero intelligentiae nostrae convenientior.
